title: Flat locally quasi-finite scheme self-relation near a finite-inertia stack point
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Schemes and affine schemes mean [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Flatness, local finite presentation and etaleness of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism]. A scheme morphism is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A scheme groupoid has the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $\mathcal X/k$ be an algebraic stack. Its inertia has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$ and arrows the isomorphisms conjugating these automorphisms; its projection forgets $\alpha$. Suppose this projection is finite, meaning every scheme base change is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For every $x\in|\mathcal X|$ [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], there are an affine $k$-scheme $U$, a morphism $p:U\to\mathcal X$ representable by algebraic spaces, flat and locally of finite presentation, and $u\in U$ mapping to $x$, such that the self $2$-fibre product $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ is a scheme. With its canonical self-relation groupoid structure, both projections $s,t:R\to U$ are separated, flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0DU4 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM-at-x), first proof paragraph and the first part of lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM to which it refers: preparation of the flat locally quasi-finite scheme self-relation. proof.text: On every scheme test $T\to\mathcal X$, the inertia base change $I_T\to T$ is a finite scheme morphism. A finite scheme map is quasi-finite, and a quasi-finite morphism is locally quasi-finite (the quasi-finite iff locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact lemma). For every etale scheme chart $V\to I_T$, the composite $V\to I_T\to T$ is then locally quasi-finite by the etale-precomposition clause of the etale source-locality lemma. A finite map is proper and in particular separated, i.e. its diagonal is a closed immersion. Thus the inertia projection has both chartwise properties. Apply the relative-inertia criterion to $\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain a locally quasi-finite diagonal. The separated-inertia implication in the separated-source lemma gives that this diagonal is separated as a representable map (a closed-immersion diagonal on tests), not that $\mathcal X$ itself is separated.

Apply the atlas theorem to obtain $q:W\to\mathcal X$ flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, with field-extension local lifting. Represent $x$ over a field $K$ and lift after $K\subset L$ to an $L$-point of $W$. Its image $w\in W$ maps to $x$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $w$ and put $p=q|_U$, $u=w$. The inclusion $U\to W$ is etale, hence smooth, flat and locally of finite presentation. Composition in the chartwise calculus gives these last two properties for $p$. It remains representable by the space-source criterion. For each scheme test $T\to\mathcal X$, $U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is the open subspace of $W\times_{\mathcal X}T$ cut out by $U\subset W$. By the open-chart lemma, every etale scheme chart $V$ of the former is also an etale scheme chart of the latter. Thus $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite by the scheme-test property of $q$. This proves the required local quasi-finiteness of $p$ without assuming that $p$ is globally surjective.

source.place: Tag 06MF; first paragraph of lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM as invoked by Tag 0DU4

proof.text: Form $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$. It is an algebraic space since $p$ is representable, using the representable pullback over a space. Each projection is a scheme base change of $p$, so flatness and local finite presentation follow from the chartwise base-change calculus. Its local quasi-finiteness follows directly from the scheme-test definition: composing any scheme chart $V\to R$ with either projection is a chart of the corresponding base change of $p$.

source.place: First proof paragraph of lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM, before the quasi-splitting step

proof.text: The map $d:R\to U\times_kU$ is the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$: on a test scheme its point is a pair $(a,b)$ with an isomorphism $p(a)\simeq p(b)$. This is exactly the diagonal comparison square. The projection $U\times_kU\to U$ is a base change of $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is separated because $U$ is affine. Separatedness is preserved by base change and composition, and for representable maps agrees with closed-immersion diagonal on tests. Therefore both composites $R\xrightarrow d U\times_kU\to U$ are separated.

source.place: First proof paragraph of lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM: separatedness of the relation projections

proof.text: Apply the separated locally quasi-finite algebraic-space representability criterion to $s:R\to U$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its target is a scheme, and steps 3--4 give precisely the chartwise local quasi-finiteness and closed-immersion diagonal required there. It gives a scheme representing $R$ over $U$. Under this identification both projections are separated, flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite scheme morphisms: the flat and local-presentation chart properties agree with their scheme versions. No quasi-compactness of $R$ is needed.

For every test scheme $T$, identify $R(T)$ with triples $(a,b,\alpha)$ where $a,b\in U(T)$ and $\alpha:p(a)\simeq p(b)$. There are no nontrivial arrows between such triples, since $U$ is a sheaf. Take $s(a,b,\alpha)=a$, $t(a,b,\alpha)=b$, unit $(a,a,1)$, inverse $(b,a,\alpha^{-1})$, and composition $(b,c,\beta)\circ(a,b,\alpha)=(a,c,\beta\alpha)$. These formulas commute with pullback and thus define morphisms of the representing schemes by Yoneda. Identity, inverse and associativity equations hold on every test scheme because they are the corresponding equations in the fibre groupoid of $\mathcal X$. This is exactly the required canonical self-relation groupoid; together with $u\mapsto x$ it finishes every clause.
